# Classification rules

Proposed rule: identify the axis of classification before assigning a label. Avoid putting subject kinds, level of abstraction, standing and evidential role into a single mutually exclusive list.

| Axis | Illustrative values |
| --- | --- |
| Subject kind | Need, requirement, system, process |
| Particularity | Kind or particular instance |
| Representation | Description, occurrence record, observation record |
| Decision/implementation standing | Proposed, accepted, implemented, evaluated |
| Evidential role | Supports, challenges, or does not address a claim |
| Scope or level | Individual, business; whole arrangement, component |

These are illustrative axes, not a settled database enum. A proposed system description can simultaneously concern a particular arrangement and support a design argument. A requirement may be high-level relative to one boundary and detailed relative to another.

Identify what is being classified. A weekly review can name a process; Monday's review is a particular execution; the page explaining how reviews work is a process description. Classifying that page as a description does not make the process itself a document. Likewise, a system description represents a system rather than becoming the operating arrangement.

Here, an **observation record** retains a representation or claim about an observation act or its result. [Observation itself is the act](../ontology/concepts/occurrences-and-state.md#what-happened-what-was-observed-and-what-was-recorded); the record's existence does not establish that the act occurred or that its claim is true. These illustrative values may overlap and do not introduce a mandatory record kind. See [patterns and ambiguity limits](../ontology/concepts/occurrences-and-state.md#observation-patterns-and-anti-patterns).

Where classification is ambiguous, preserve the ambiguity and name the question. Do not force a single bucket merely to fit a directory. Domains such as health remain optional grouping proposals; ontology/taxonomy/mereology are modeling views rather than domain primitives.

See [ontology](../../../source-locators.md#source-5a5f0f2c1d016afb) for definitions. F1 and EOM-01 remain open in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a): this draft records the remedy but does not establish its completeness.
